title: Второй шанс и угроза Никиты  (A Second Chance and Nikita's Threat)

segments.t: Patrick Malouda confides that he too was once a promising chef until an injury ended his kitchen career, and he agrees to return in the evening so Viktor can cook for him. Outside, a bitter Nikita confronts Denis after the canceled wedding.
Вы с Катей из-за меня расстались?
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
'Believe me, I know what that is like.' The inspector picks a warm view in front of Denis, anchoring the Russian line on "poverte" ("believe") and "znayu" ("know") without extra filler.
'Once I too was a chef.' The inspector sustains a frank manner toward Nikita, pairing "kogda-to" ("once, at one time") with "tozhe" ("too") to get the point across in plain spoken Russian.

'Because of an injury I had to leave the profession.' The inspector picks a firm stance as the scene unfolds, weaving "travmy" ("injury, trauma") together with "prishlos" ("had to, it fell to") just the way native speakers do.
'Unfortunately, such is our life.' The inspector favors an earnest tempo for Nikita, leaning on "sozhaleniyu" ("regret") before closing the thought with "takova" ("such is").
'Maybe you will come to us once more?' Denis queries naturally to keep things clear, joining "mozhet" ("can") to "yeshchyo" ("more, still") so every word pulls its weight.

'Viktor will definitely surprise you today.' Denis sustains a natural direction as the scene unfolds, linking "obyazatelno" ("surely, without fail"), "segodnya" ("today"), and "udivit" ("to surprise") in one brisk exchange.
'Yes, I will come with great pleasure.' The inspector strikes a serious tempo across the room, weaving "pridu" ("will come") together with "bolshim" ("great") just the way native speakers do.
Вы с Катей из-за меня расстались?
'Did you and Katya break up because of me?' Nikita tests evenly for the inspector's benefit, linking "rasstalis" ("broke up, separated"), "vy" ("you"), and "katey" ("Katya") in one brisk exchange.
'I wanted the two of you to get married.' Denis offers an emphatic angle in the room, weaving "khotel" ("wanted") together with "pozhenilis" ("to married") just the way native speakers do.
'Yes, you tried very hard.' Nikita displays a steady posture in front of the inspector, anchoring the Russian line on "ochen" ("very much") and "silno" ("strongly, much") without extra filler.
'Especially that evening on the roof.' Nikita strikes a brisk stance as the scene unfolds, combining "osobenno" ("especially") and "togda" ("back then") so the key meaning lands right away.
'I made inquiries about you.' Nikita chooses a brisk rhythm in their talk, pairing "navyol" ("to establish") with "spravki" ("inquiries") to get the point across in plain spoken Russian.
Вы с Катей из-за меня расстались?
Nikita remarks that Denis has a talent for making enemies—and moments later, thugs arrive to settle an old score with Denis. See you next time!
